title: Energy Interactions — 12-Mark Preparation
note: Original ACADRIX practice questions based on the R-2025 Unit III syllabus. These are not claimed to be official university questions or PYQs.

questions.question: Explain the concept of a thermodynamic system, surroundings and boundary. Classify systems as closed, open and isolated systems and give suitable mechanical-engineering examples.
solutionPlan: Define system, surroundings and boundary.
Explain closed, open and isolated systems.
Compare mass and energy interactions for each type.
Give practical engineering examples.

questions.question: Explain the different modes of energy transfer associated with an engineering system and distinguish heat transfer from work transfer with suitable examples.
solutionPlan: Introduce energy interaction across a system boundary.
Define heat and work as energy-transfer modes.
Explain mechanical and thermal examples.
Highlight the distinction between heat and work.

questions.question: Explain heat conduction and derive the one-dimensional Fourier law of heat conduction. Discuss the effect of thermal conductivity, area and temperature gradient.
solutionPlan: Define conduction and thermal conductivity.
State Fourier law and explain its sign convention.
Write the heat-transfer-rate relation.
Discuss the influence of k, A and temperature gradient.

questions.question: Explain convection heat transfer and derive/use Newton's law of cooling. Differentiate natural convection and forced convection with engineering applications.
solutionPlan: Define convection and the fluid boundary layer concept.
State Newton's law of cooling.
Explain the convection coefficient and temperature difference.
Compare natural and forced convection with examples.

questions.question: Explain thermal radiation, blackbody radiation and emissivity. State the Stefan–Boltzmann relation and discuss why radiation heat transfer can occur through a vacuum.
solutionPlan: Define thermal radiation and electromagnetic energy transfer.
Explain blackbody and emissivity.
State the Stefan–Boltzmann relation.
Explain radiation through vacuum and practical applications.

questions.question: Compare conduction, convection and radiation in terms of physical mechanism, medium requirement, governing relation and engineering applications.
solutionPlan: Define the three modes.
Compare their physical mechanisms and medium requirements.
Write the principal relations used in the syllabus.
Give representative mechanical-engineering applications.

questions.question: Explain the working principle of a heat engine. Derive the relation between heat supplied, heat rejected and net work output, and obtain the thermal-efficiency expression.
solutionPlan: Define heat engine and identify source, engine and sink.
Apply the energy balance to obtain net work.
Define thermal efficiency.
Interpret the efficiency relation physically.

questions.question: Explain the working principle of a refrigerator and define coefficient of performance (COP). Describe the basic vapour-compression refrigeration cycle and the function of its main components.
solutionPlan: Define refrigeration and COP of a refrigerator.
Explain the vapour-compression cycle in sequence.
Describe compressor, condenser, expansion device and evaporator.
Relate the cycle to domestic and industrial refrigeration.

questions.question: Explain the working principle of a heat pump and compare it with a refrigerator. Establish the relationship between COP of a heat pump and COP of a refrigerator.
solutionPlan: Define heat pump and refrigerator.
Explain their common reversed-heat-engine cycle.
Distinguish useful heat output from useful cooling effect.
Establish COPHP = COPR + 1.

questions.question: With a neat schematic representation, explain the sequence of processes in a basic vapour-compression refrigeration system and describe the energy interaction at each major component.
solutionPlan: Draw the four principal components and flow direction.
Explain compression, condensation, expansion and evaporation.
Identify heat/work interactions at each component.
Summarize the complete cycle and cooling effect.

questions.question: Explain the purpose and basic functions of an HVAC system. Discuss heating, ventilation, air conditioning and thermal-comfort considerations in buildings and engineering facilities.
solutionPlan: Define HVAC and its objectives.
Explain heating, cooling and ventilation functions.
Discuss temperature, humidity and air movement as comfort considerations.
Give building and industrial applications.

questions.question: A hot engineering surface loses heat to surrounding air. Explain how you would identify whether conduction, convection or radiation is involved and formulate the appropriate heat-transfer relation for each mechanism.
solutionPlan: Identify the system boundary and heat-flow path.
Recognize conduction within solids, convection at fluid interfaces and radiation to surroundings.
Write Fourier, Newton-cooling and Stefan–Boltzmann relations as applicable.
Explain how combined heat-transfer paths may occur.

questions.question: Compare a heat engine, refrigerator and heat pump based on purpose, direction of heat transfer, work interaction and performance measure. Explain their relationship as energy-conversion devices.
solutionPlan: Define all three devices.
Compare heat flow and work input/output.
State efficiency or COP as appropriate.
Explain the common thermodynamic-energy interaction concept.

questions.question: Discuss the role of heat transfer and refrigeration/HVAC systems in mechanical engineering. Explain suitable applications in manufacturing, automobiles, buildings and industrial equipment.
solutionPlan: Identify thermal-management needs in mechanical systems.
Explain relevant heat-transfer modes.
Discuss refrigeration and HVAC applications.
Connect thermal systems to efficiency, safety and operating performance.

questions.question: Develop an integrated explanation of energy interactions in a mechanical engineering thermal system, beginning with the system boundary and heat transfer and extending to heat engines, refrigeration and HVAC applications.
solutionPlan: Start with system, surroundings and boundary.
Explain heat/work interactions.
Connect conduction, convection and radiation to thermal equipment.
Relate these concepts to heat engines, refrigeration and HVAC systems.
Conclude with practical engineering significance.
